commit e92bd573e2cf3f494139720d11000f0a7c3e8b0b
Author: Yulong Han <wheatfox17@icloud.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 27 00:10:17 2026 +0800

    ci(webots): run the suite once per scene backend
    
    Scene ships two perception backends, but CI only ever exercised one. It
    ran whichever image the runner happened to have: a hand-built
    robonix-scene-dualmap image without a DualMap checkout, so the backend
    selection fell back to ConceptGraphs without saying so and DualMap was
    never tested.
    
    The Webots job now runs as a matrix over concept_graphs and dualmap. Each
    leg names its backend and image explicitly, and a step reads the backend
    the running scene reports and fails the leg when it is not the one asked
    for. The DualMap image is built over the fresh scene image and tagged by
    the hash of its Dockerfile and base image, so it is rebuilt only when one
    of them changes. Its Dockerfile takes GitHub and Hugging Face mirror
    prefixes, which the runner needs: large transfers from it to both sites
    get cut off mid-stream.
    
    Artifacts, reports and report site entries carry the backend key, so the
    two legs publish separately instead of overwriting each other.
    
    A runner killed mid-job never reaches its cleanup and leaves ci-*
    containers holding the GPU, which made the next run fail the GPU capacity
    check. The runner takes one job at a time, so the job now removes every
    ci-* container, image, volume and network before it waits for the GPU.
    
    The scenario runner counted any failed leaf as unexpected, even in a step
    that declares retry_delay_s and so is meant to fail and be served again.
    After the lifecycle restart, object_navigation picks an object Scene still
    remembers while SLAM is rebuilding the map from scratch; the first plan
    toward it can fail until the map covers it, and the retry then succeeds.
    The runner now tolerates the failed attempts of a retryable step that a
    later round satisfied, and the navigate step declares retry_delay_s. A
    step that never succeeds still fails the scenario.
    
    The DualMap leg then timed out in object_navigation. DualMap put the
    target plant on a wall, and goal_near searched rings around it in the
    order of distance to the preferred approach direction only, so the first
    footprint-clear cell it found was behind the wall, in space the robot had
    never seen. Nav2 chased that goal around the building until the scenario
    timed out. object_goal now takes a cell on the robot's side of the target
    whenever one fits within a metre of the nearest far-side cell, and falls
    back to the far side only when the near side has no room.
---

+# Robonix CI bot — ChatOps front-end for the GPU testing pipeline.
+#
+# A maintainer comments `@robonix-ci test` on a pull request; this workflow
+# runs the full testing.yml pipeline on the self-hosted GPU runner and edits a
+# single status comment with the pass rate, the failing cases, and where the
+# logs are. No separate hosted bot/server — GitHub Actions IS the bot.
+#
+# ─────────────────────────── SECURITY (read first) ───────────────────────────
+# `issue_comment` runs with the BASE repo's token, so the trigger is gated hard:
+#   1. Only PR comments (not plain issues) whose body starts with the command.
+#   2. Only callers with actual repo permission `admin` or `maintain` may
+#      start a run. A drive-by commenter, org member without repo admin/maintain,
+#      or write-only contributor cannot start work on the self-hosted runner.
+#   3. The actual GPU job still goes through testing.yml's `security-gate` +
+#      `environment: gpu-testing` (required-reviewer approval, once configured),
+#      so even an
+#      authorized comment pauses for a human before touching the 5090.
+
+name: Robonix CI Bot
+
+on:
+  issue_comment:
+    types: [created]
+
+permissions:
+  actions: read
+  contents: write
+  pull-requests: write
+  issues: write
+

+  gate:
+    name: Authorize CI command

+      github.event.issue.pull_request &&

+      merge_ref_available: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.merge_ref_available }}
+      pr_base_ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.base_ref }}
+      pr_number: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}
+      pr_title: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.title }}
+      pr_author: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.author }}
+      pr_url: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.url }}
+      pr_head_ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.head_ref }}
+      pr_head_repo: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.head_repo }}
+      pr_head_sha: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.head_sha }}
+      triggered_by: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.triggered_by }}
+      comment_id: ${{ steps.say.outputs.comment_id }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Authorize caller permission
+        id: auth
+        uses: actions/github-script@v7
+        with:
+          script: |
+            const username = context.payload.comment.user.login;
+            let permission = 'none';
+            try {
+              const r = await github.rest.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel({
+                owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, username,
+              });
+              permission = r.data.role_name || r.data.permission || 'none';
+            } catch (e) {
+              core.notice(`could not resolve repo permission for @${username}: ${e.message}`);
+            }
+            const authorized = ['admin', 'maintain'].includes(permission);
+            core.setOutput('permission', permission);
+            core.setOutput('authorized', String(authorized));
+            if (!authorized) {
+              core.notice(`@${username} has repo permission '${permission}', not allowed to run robonix CI`);
+            }
